verdict.rationale: Railway's own marketing directly says HTTP, TCP, gRPC, and WebSockets are "handled automatically," and that public endpoints, SSL, and load balancing are live from deploy, which implies no per-protocol setup. The evidence is a single homepage line, though, with no technical docs showing all four protocols served at once from one deployed service. Missing for 10: documentation that one service can expose HTTP, TCP, gRPC, and WebSocket together, details of how the protocols are exposed (e.g. TCP proxying or ports), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve HTTP, TCP, gRPC, and WebSocket traffic from the same deployed service without separate protocol configuration

citations.quote: HTTP, TCP, gRPC, WebSockets handled automatically.
Private connections, public endpoints, SSL, and load balancing live from the moment you deploy.
